title: GPU node-fleet module: mixed-instance + MIG-aware upgrade safety + health hooks for Private VPC
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
Develop a reusable Terraform module for Private (VPC) GPU node-fleets that supports mixed-instance groups (multiple GPU SKUs/instance types), optional ASG or Karpenter provisioners, and safe in-place MIG/driver upgrade flows with health hooks tailored for constrained VPC environments (ENI/IP limits, single-tenant subnets).

Problem statement:
We need a single, well-documented module that platform teams can use to create GPU capacity pools in customer VPCs with predictable scaling and safe upgrade behavior. Current modules are fragmented and do not handle: mixed-instance placement, MIG partitioning lifecycle, differences between ASG and Karpenter drain/termination semantics, preflight validation for per-subnet ENI/address limits, or a canary path for driver and runtime upgrades. Failures during driver upgrades have caused customer infra incidents and extended outages in Private deployments.

Goals:
- Expose a Terraform module API that lets callers specify: list of instance types (by GPU class), desired MIG configs (per-instance family), node labels/taints, provisioner type (ASG|Karpenter), desired autoscaling policy, and upgrade strategy (canary %/AZs, rolling batch sizes).
- Implement lifecycle hooks and node health checks to gate driver & MIG upgrades (pre-drain integration tests, post-cordon KV-cache validation for inference workloads).
- Add preflight 'terraform plan' validations and a small CLI helper (bash/Go) that verifies subnet ENI/IP headroom, instance quota, and driver image availability in the private registry before apply.
- Support graceful fallbacks: if Karpenter provisioner is unavailable, fallback to ASG headroom provider and surface telemetry for routing capacity.
- Produce automated integration tests that run in our private test VPCs and verify: scaling, MIG partitioning, graceful drain, successful driver rollouts, and canary rollback semantics.

Design notes / approach:
- Module surface: terraform module that creates either an ASG-based launch-template-backed node group OR Karpenter provisioner CRDs (via eks add-on or helm). Use a single input variable 'provisioner_mode' to toggle paths.
- Mixed-instances: accept a prioritized list of instance families (e.g., [a10g, a100, t4]) with optional weights and an affinity preference for AZs to mitigate ENI exhaustion. Provide optional spot/ondemand mixes with graceful eviction handling.
- MIG-aware upgrades: include a stateful probe that runs a driver pre-check and a MIG partition reconcile hook. Upgrade flow: 1) create canary nodes in single AZ and run health checks; 2) if canary passes, drain batch of nodes (respecting batch_size and max_unavailable), run post-upgrade verification (runtime self-check and a small inference probe using a pinned model); 3) if verification fails, auto-rollback the driver package on the batch and mark rollout as failed.
- Health hooks: add Terraform module outputs that link to Lambda or SSM runbooks for driver install/rollback and integrate with our Console rollouts to annotate progress. Health checks: node kubelet + driver plugin readiness, NVML / MIG device count match, and a lightweight inference scorer (local container) that uses cached KV to validate end-to-end inference on warmed model.
- Preflight validations: implement a 'validate_private_vpc.sh' wrapper that runs: subnet ENI headroom check, instance quota check, AMI/driver image fetch test from private registry, and IAM permission minimum set. The module will optionally call the validation via external data source during 'terraform plan' (opt-in to avoid noisy RPCs).
- Observability: emit CloudWatch/Prometheus metrics (node_create_time, driver_install_duration, canary_result, rollback_count) and structured events for Console to consume.

Acceptance criteria:
- Terraform module published to registry with docs and example private VPC usage.
- Module supports toggling between Karpenter and ASG paths with identical public inputs.
- Demonstrated canary driver rollout in staging VPC with automatic rollback on failed probe.
- Preflight validation script available and included in README; run in CI on each PR touching module.
- Integration tests in CI that validate scaling, drain behavior, and MIG partitioning for at least one GPU family.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: module skeleton + API surface + README + unit tests for input validation.
- Week 2: implement ASG path (launch template, lifecycle hooks), health-check probes, and preflight script.
- Week 3: implement Karpenter integration path and fallback logic; wire metrics and Console events.
- Week 4: run integration tests, shepherd internal migration (2 internal customers), and publish module version with upgrade notes.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: ENI/IP exhaustion during canary or scale-up. Mitigation: preflight check and per-AZ allocation limits; prefer cross-AZ placement for canaries.
- Risk: Karpenter semantics differ per cluster version. Mitigation: pin EKS/kubernetes compatibility matrix in module and add E2E tests for supported combos.
- Risk: driver installation failures cause stuck nodes. Mitigation: automated rollback hook and drain timeout with auto-terminate and replace policy.

Implementation artifacts to link in comments below (PRs, RFCs, design docs).
